title: Strict cohomology bound for subclusters of a general section
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $C$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes with completed local rings $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $h^i(C,F)=\dim_k H^i(C,F)$ for Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Suppose that $\deg_k(L|_B)\geq 2p_a(B)+1$ for every nonempty reduced union $B$ of irreducible components, including disconnected unions and $B=C$, where $p_a(B)=1-\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then there exists $s\in H^0(C,L)$ such that its zero scheme $S=Z(s)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] is finite, reduced, and supported in the smooth locus, and $s$ is nonzero at the generic point of every irreducible component. For every nonempty closed subscheme $T\subseteq S$, with ideal sheaf $I_T\subseteq\mathcal O_C$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], one has
$$h^0(C,I_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}L)+h^1(C,I_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}L)<h^0(C,L).$$
Tensor products use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A finite reduced subscheme here is a finite disjoint union of reduced closed $k$-points; no assertion is made for $T=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], and properness includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the curve is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and has finitely many components [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Invertible modules are finite locally free, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; their cohomology is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-coherent-hi]. Every reduced component union is again projective and nodal by [lem-sfb-nodal-subcurve-dualizing-annihilator], and the same facts apply on each connected component. The functorial long exact cohomology sequence is available by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact], since module sheaves have enough injectives and global sections is left exact [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives, lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact].

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text: Let $D$ be any nonempty connected projective reduced curve, nodal as in the item, and $A$ any invertible module on $D$ with $\deg(A|_B)\geq2p_a(B)+1$ for every nonempty reduced union $B$ of components of $D$; for instance $D\subseteq C$ a connected reduced subcurve and $A=L|_D$. For every connected reduced subcurve $B$ of $D$, proper reduced global functions are $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product]. Together with vanishing above dimension one [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension], this gives $p_a(B)=h^1(B,\mathcal O_B)\geq0$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction] to $D$, $A$ and the empty cluster: if $H^1(D,A)$ were nonzero, a connected reduced subcurve $B\subseteq D$ would have $\deg(A|_B)\leq2p_a(B)-2$, contradicting the numerical hypothesis. Hence $H^1(D,A)=0$; this is the vanishing used for empty clusters in steps 4, 5 and 7. In particular, writing $d=\deg L$ and $g=p_a(C)$, [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch] gives $h^0(C,L)=d+1-g$.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-nodal-numerical-very-ample], the complete linear system embeds $C$. Apply [lem-zl-bertini-smooth-member] on its smooth locus, using the restriction of the full section space; the induced morphism is the restriction of this closed immersion. This gives a nonempty open of section coefficients whose zero scheme on the smooth locus is smooth. There are finitely many nodes: [lem-trf-reduced-curve-normalization-genus] gives a finite normalization quotient support. Off this support the finite normalization map is an isomorphism: on affine opens its algebra equals the structure algebra. Its source is a disjoint union of smooth curves by the same node, so this open is smooth, so every node lies in that finite support. Remove the hyperplanes of sections vanishing at those nodes and at one smooth closed point on each component. Each hyperplane is proper by generation. Intersecting these opens with the Bertini open remains nonempty; over infinite algebraically closed $k$ it has a $k$-point (a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on all $k^r$, by induction on $r$). Choose $s$ there. Its zero scheme $S$ is closed, contains no component and avoids the nodes; it is therefore zero-dimensional, and [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] makes it finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] its zero-dimensional local rings are regular, hence fields: dimension zero means their maximal ideals need zero generators. Their residue fields are $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Thus $S$ is reduced, smooth-supported, and $s$ is nonzero at every component generic point.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text: We prove the stronger inductive assertion: for every connected projective nodal $D$ with fewer than or equal to the given number of components, every line $A$ satisfying the numerical bounds, every section $a$ whose zero divisor is finite reduced and avoids all nodes, and every nonempty subset $T$ of that divisor, one has $h^1(D,A(-T))<|T|/2$. For the empty subset use $h^1(D,A)=0$ from step 2. Since a subscheme of a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a subset, this covers all clusters in the item. Locally at $T$ the ideal is generated by a uniformizer of a smooth curve; elsewhere it is the unit ideal. Hence $A(-T)=I_T\otimes A$ is invertible and the section $a$ gives a section of it nonzero at every generic point. The zero-scheme ideal convention is [def-pc-zero-scheme]. Strong induction starts with one component; the cases below either use fewer components or close the argument directly.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text: Put $M=A(-T)$, $t=|T|>0$. If $h^1(D,M)=0$, the inductive assertion holds. Otherwise apply [lem-sfb-nodal-dual-support-dichotomy]. In alternative (2), decompose the proper subcurve $Y$ into connected components $Y_j$. Each has fewer components, and the restricted section has zero scheme $S\cap Y_j$, still reduced and smooth-supported. The degree hypothesis on every subcurve of $Y_j$ is inherited from $D$. Set $t_j=|T\cap Y_j|$. Induction gives $h^1(Y_j,M|_{Y_j})<t_j/2$ for $t_j>0$, and step 2 gives zero for $t_j=0$. Cohomology on this finite disjoint union is the direct sum: sheaves and injective resolutions decompose componentwise. If all $t_j=0$, the equality in alternative (2) contradicts $h^1(D,M)>0$. Otherwise summing gives $h^1(D,M)<\sum_jt_j/2\leq t/2$.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text:
In the remaining case there is a map $M\to\omega_D$ generically nonzero on every component. If every nontrivial component partition meets in at least two nodes, [lem-sfb-nodal-two-connected-clifford] applies: $M$ has the generically nonzero section from step 4 as well as this map. It gives $h^0(D,M)\leq\deg M/2+1$. The sequence $0\to M\to A\to A|_T\to0$ and [lem-pc-euler-additive, lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] show $\deg M=d_D-t$, where $d_D=\deg A$. Riemann--Roch [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch] now gives
$$h^1(D,M)\leq g_D-d_D/2+t/2<t/2,$$
because $d_D\geq2g_D+1$. This includes the one-component base case.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text:
Otherwise a component partition meets in exactly one node $p$: the curve is connected, so it cannot meet in zero nodes. Write its two sides $D_1,D_2$. By [lem-trf-stacks-nodal-closed-subcurve] the intersection is reduced and the point is smooth on each side. Both sides are connected; a disconnected side would have a component disjoint from the other side and from its own remaining components. Each has fewer irreducible components and inherits the numerical hypothesis. The closed-union identity of [lem-trf-closed-union-pushout], tensored locally with a frame of $M$, gives
$$0\to M\to (i_1)_*(M|_{D_1})\oplus(i_2)_*(M|_{D_2})\to M|_p\to0,$$
where the last arrow is the difference of the two fibre values. Since $p$ is a node and $T$ avoids nodes, the section $a$ is nonzero at $p$; its restriction to $D_1$ makes this last arrow surjective on global sections. The long exact sequence (step 1), and vanishing of positive cohomology of the skyscraper [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support], give
$$h^1(D,M)=h^1(D_1,M|_{D_1})+h^1(D_2,M|_{D_2}).$$
[lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] identifies cohomology of each closed pushforward with that on its subcurve. Induction on each nonempty $T\cap D_i$ and step 2 for an empty one give the strict bound, since $t_1+t_2=t>0$. This completes strong induction.

source.place: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 proof, printed pp.47--49; nodal reconstruction. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online.

proof.text:
Apply the inductive assertion with $D=C$, $A=L$, $a=s$. For nonempty $T\subseteq S$, let $t=|T|$ and $M=I_T\otimes L$. The exact ideal quotient sequence and Euler additivity, with the zero-dimensional quotient of Euler characteristic $t$, give
$$\chi(M)=\chi(L)-t=h^0(C,L)-t,$$
using $H^1(C,L)=0$ from step 2. By nodal Riemann--Roch,
$$h^0(C,M)+h^1(C,M)=h^0(C,L)-t+2h^1(C,M)<h^0(C,L).$$
The section chosen in step 3 has every required geometric property. The argument makes no claim for $t=0$, where strictness would be false.

The item is FT 4.1 for nodal curves, with the T=∅ case correctly excluded; the statement is unchanged. Steps 1-8 checked. Bertini is applied on the smooth locus, and its immersion and generation hypotheses hold. The node count is finite via the normalization support. The strong induction is set up correctly. The dichotomy case uses induction on the connected components of Y. The Clifford case gives h1<=g-d/2+t/2<t/2. The separating-node case uses the ring fibre-product sequence, a(p)≠0 and H1 additivity. Step 8 is the χ computation. New nodes: numerical-very-ample = FT 2.5(iii)/CFHR, true. Dual-support dichotomy proved independently: if no map has full support, V=∪V_i over infinite k gives V=V_i, and I_Y·I_{C_i}=0 plus the annihilator node and duality give h1(X)=h1(Y). The two-connected Clifford node is exactly Thm 2.7 for Cartier subcanonical Z with M=I_Zω, since nodal length equals A·B. All three were tested on small cases; none is a duplicate or a restated clause, and all have B1-B7 form.
